university.summary: ICHEC Brussels Management School is a leading business school in Brussels with a strong international network, offering exchange programs for students from partner universities. The school emphasizes global outlook, academic excellence, and sustainable development, with two campuses located in the heart of Brussels. Exchange students are welcomed to participate in various student associations and cultural activities.
strengths: ICHEC is a member of prestigious academic networks including AACSB, CLADEA, EFMD, CFA, Conférence des HEC francophones, NIBES, and Pôle Louvain. It has over 3000 students from 60 nationalities and 10,000 alumni. The school offers a wide range of management programs in French and English, with a focus on sustainable development and business ethics. Exchange students can benefit from the school's strong network of international organizations and companies in Brussels.
facilities: ICHEC has two campuses in downtown Brussels: Montgomery Campus (Boulevard Brand Whitlock, 2, 1150 Brussels) and Anjou Campus (Rue au Bois, 365A, 1150 Brussels). The Montgomery Campus houses the library and a new cafeteria. The Anjou Campus is located in a green area near a Sport Center and is where the International Office is situated. The school offers weekly French lessons at beginner, intermediate, and advanced levels.
student_life: Student life at ICHEC is rich with many active student associations covering culture, sport, folklore, charity, entrepreneurship, and sustainable development. Exchange students are encouraged to join associations such as the Student Council (Conseil des Etudiants), ESN-ICHEC (Erasmus Student Network), AIESEC-ICHEC, OIKOS, CICHEC, and ICHEC Junior Consult. The ESN-ICHEC offers support for administrative and academic procedures, organizes festive and cultural events, and creates WhatsApp groups for incoming students. The CICHEC offers job services and various social events including Miss ICHEC, Welcome night, ICHEC Ball, and D100 Party.
local_life: Brussels is located at the heart of Europe, close to European Union administrations and international organizations. The city is the center of a wide European market with excellent transportation connections to Paris, London, Köln, and Amsterdam. Brussels is home to the European Commission and NATO institutions, and hosts over a thousand international companies. The city is known for its rich architectural heritage (e.g., medieval Bruges) and cultural traditions, including folk festivals in Ghent. Belgian gastronomy is diverse, with special Belgian beers being among the best in the world. Brussels is divided into 19 communes, with recommended areas for accommodation including residential areas (1140 Evere, 1200 Woluwe-Saint-Lambert, 1150 Woluwe-Saint-Pierre, 1160 Auderghem, 1170 Watermael-Boitsfort, 1180 Uccle) and animated areas (1000 Bruxelles, 1030 Schaerbeek, 1040 Etterbeek, 1050 Ixelles).

exchange_program.application_process: Contact International Office (exchange.in@ichec.be) for application. Learning Agreement should be sent to Mrs. Kristien Minet by June 15 (for 1st semester) and December 15 (for 2nd semester).
exchange_program.course_registration_notes: Learning Agreement should be sent to Mrs. Kristien Minet at latest on June 15 (for 1st semester) and December 15 (for 2nd semester). Students can change study programme during first week of semester.

additional_requirements.extracted_notes: Erasmus+ students must use online EWP Learning Agreement. Non-Erasmus students can use ICHEC learning agreement template. Minimum language recommendation: B2 level in English/French depending on language of classes. Intensive week of French available before each semester (Sept 8-12, 2025 and Jan 27-31, 2026).

course_restrictions: All ICHEC courses are open to exchange students. Students can choose any course from BAC1 to MASTER2, in French, English, during day or evening. Complete course list available via https://www.ichec.be/en/inward-exchanges

academic_periods.notes: Orientation day on first day of semester; ESN-ICHEC welcome week during first week
Optional intensive week of French (3 ECTS, 30h/week) before Fall semester
Optional intensive week of French (3 ECTS, 30h/week) before Spring semester
